newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B index ends down on new crackdown rumours.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B index ends down on new crackdown rumours.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index ended down marginally on Thursday with rumours of new crackdown measures swirling around the market despite institutional support for big shares, brokers said.
The B index fell 0.292 points or 0.34 percent to 86.340 points on volume of 16.687 million shares worth $11.842 million.
According to the rumours, specific measures on how to bar state-owned enterprises from "speculative" stock trading would be worked out in the short term, brokers said.
"Rumours of further clampdown measures prevailed the market again late in the session, which triggered a little selling to unwind positions and pushed down the index," said one broker.
"The new issue of Jinan Qingqi Motocycle also sucked some capital from the secondary markek," another broker said.

Jinan Qingqi Motorcycle began issuing 230 million B shares today at a price of $0.482 per share for listing on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, a company statement in Thursday's Shanghai Securities News said.
Of 43 B shares, 39 traded, with 23 down, four flat and 12 up.
Shanghai Jinjiang Tower was the biggest loser on unpromising prospects, plunging $0.032 or 9.19 percent to $0.316 on volume of 108,000 shares.

Pudong real estate firm Shanghai Jinqiao Export Processing Zone Development was the most actively traded with some institutions seen liquidating their positions after prices rose in the morning on news that a major micro-chip project located in the area had been signed in Beijing.
It ended down $0.006 or 0.83 percent at $0.714 on volume of 3.4 million shares.
Shanghai's A share index fell late in the session on the same rumours, triggering heavy selling to unwind positions, brokers said.
The index fell 7.390 points or 0.56 percent to 1,318.645 on volume of 435.0 million shares worth 6.3 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index dipped 26.501 points or 0.67 percent to 3,913.154 points.
Beijing Lightbus fell the most on institutional selling, slipping 0.45 yuan or 6.95 percent to 6.02 yuan on volume of 1.7 million shares.
